tooley.q: A Level C software classification is one in which a failure could result in:
opts: fatal injuries to passengers or crew
minor injuries to passengers or crew
aircraft loss
tooley.explain: Table 13.1: level C is a major failure: workload impairs crew efficiency, occupant discomfort including injuries. Aircraft loss is level A; serious or fatal injury is level B.

tooley.q: A Level B software classification is one in which the probability of failure is:
opts: extremely remote
remote
extremely improbable
tooley.explain: Table 13.1: A is extremely improbable (below 10⁻⁹), B is extremely remote (10⁻⁹ to 10⁻⁷), C is remote (10⁻⁷ to 10⁻⁵).

tooley.q: A software configuration management plan must be created and maintained by:
opts: the CAA or FAA
the aircraft operator
the relevant DO
tooley.explain: Tooley 13.2: the CMP must be devised and maintained by the relevant DO and be effective throughout the life of the equipment.

tooley.q: Weather radar is an example of:
opts: Class B software
Class C software
Class D software
tooley.explain: Table 13.2: level D includes AHRS automatic levelling, CMC/CFDIU, data loader and weather radar.

tooley.q: Electronic engine control software is an example of:
opts: LSAP
DFLD
OSS
tooley.explain: The EEC is a typical LSAP target (with DFDAU, APU ECU, FGC). DFLD is data; OSS is typical of IMA units.

tooley.q: OSS and UMS are specific classes of:
opts: DFLD
LSAP
FLS
tooley.explain: FLS (field loadable software) has three types: LSAP, UMS and OSS.

tooley.q: The final stage of loading EEC software is:
opts: verifying the loaded software
switching on and testing the system
disconnecting the PDL
tooley.explain: After removing the loader and reconnecting the cables, run the memory verification program (PASS for part number and checksums), then mark the plate (steps 9 and 10).

floyd.q: With the BCD code 0111 and EVEN parity, the parity bit is:
opts: Undetermined
floyd.explain: 0111 has three 1s (odd), so the even parity bit must be 1 to make four (even). Matches Table 2-8 (P = 1 for 0111).

floyd.q: What can a parity bit detect?
opts: Any error whatsoever occurring in the group
A single bit error (or an odd number of errors) in the group
Two bit errors within the same group
floyd.explain: Floyd: parity detects a single bit error (or any odd number of errors) but cannot check for two errors in one group.

floyd.q: In Floyd's CRC example with D = 11010011 and G = 1010, the transmitted code is:
floyd.explain: Append four zeros, divide modulo-2 by 1010 to get remainder 0100; replacing the four zeros with 0100 gives 110100110100. Dividing again by 1010 leaves 0 (checked in code in the notebook).

floyd.q: The receiver divides the received data by the generator code G and finds a NON-ZERO remainder. This means:
opts: Append zeros and divide once more
There is no error, the data is accepted
A transmission error is detected, request retransmission
floyd.explain: Step 7 of Floyd's CRC process: a non-zero remainder means an error has been detected and the receiver requests retransmission.

floyd.q: According to Floyd, how is the checksum in the ROM test example produced?
opts: Summing each column of bits and discarding carries (XOR of each column)
Dividing the ROM contents by a fixed generator code
Multiplying all the words and keeping the low 8 bits
floyd.explain: Floyd 11-11: the checksum is the sum of each column of data bits discarding the carries, i.e. the XOR sum of each column (Figure 11-74).

Level D

generated.q: An FLS upgrade may have been corrupted during transfer. What should be done?
opts: Try loading it once to see whether the software runs normally before deciding
Load it and rely only on the LOAD COMPLETE message to conclude it is good
Quarantine it and hold it pending the supplier's integrity or version checks
generated.explain: Tooley 13.3, Key Point box and Test 13.6: if in doubt do not attempt the transfer, quarantine it.

generated.q: Which release document usually accompanies a navigation database DFLD?
opts: Only an ordinary Certificate of Conformity
An EASA Form 1 or FAA 8130-3 as for an LSAP
Letter of Acceptance or an equivalent
generated.explain: Tooley 13.3.3: an EASA Form 1 or FAA 8130-3 cannot be provided for navigation database DFLD, so a Letter of Acceptance is used.

generated.q: A file has 5 bytes 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. The 8-bit checksum (sum mod 256) is:
Two bytes of a file are swapped. A simple additive checksum will:
opts: always be 0, so the file is reported valid
stay the same, so the error is not detected
always change, so the error is always detected
generated.explain: Addition is commutative so byte order does not affect the sum. A CRC does (Demo 1).

be a different version for the left and right engines
be write-protected
